dedupe_keys.name: flowsdt geospatial digital twin for urban flood dynamics galveston texas

description: FlowsDT is a geospatial digital twin of Galveston, a Texas barrier island, built to analyse and communicate pluvial and fluvial flood hazards at street and basement level. The study creates FlowsDT-Galveston on 1D-2D coupled hydrodynamic models in PCSWMM, integrating topography, hydrography and infrastructure, LiDAR, land cover and storm sewer geometry, validates it with historical flood events and social sensing, and models hyperlocal flooding for 2-, 10-, 25-, 50- and 100-year return period rainfall in a four-dimensional environment. Results show buildings inundated over one foot increase by 5.7 percent and roads inundated over one foot by 6.7 percent from the 2-year to the 100-year flood. The authors say the framework can be extended to other communities. Coverage: one city, design storm scenarios. Access: free preprint; software or data release and interfaces are not stated on the page read; the paper is CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the abstract does not say whether the twin is public or run in real time. It supports urban flood digital twin and scenario studies, and relates to EPA SWMM in the catalogue.
